balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Netwealth Group Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Netwealth Group Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Netwealth Group Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Netwealth Group Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fua.title: Funds Under Administration (FUA)
fua.content:
FUA is the total value of client assets held on Netwealth's platform -- the balance its platform and administration fees are charged against. It is reported annually only, not at half-year, and is roughly 4x the smaller AUM figure (assets Netwealth itself manages within that FUA).

For Netwealth Group Limited: FUA growth, not revenue growth, is the primary driver investors and management track -- revenue follows FUA at a margin (see Platform Revenue Margin) that is slowly compressing as scale and competition increase.

What to watch:

  • FUA growth versus net flows -- the gap is market movement, not new money
  • Custodial FUA (on-platform) versus the small non-custodial/advised sliver

fuaFlows.title: FUA inflows, outflows and net flows
fuaFlows.content:
Inflows and outflows are custodial client money moving onto and off the platform; net flows is the difference -- organic growth before market movement.

For Netwealth Group Limited: this is the number management highlights every half -- net flows as a percentage of opening FUA is the organic growth rate the market prices the stock on, separate from market-driven FUA appreciation.

What to watch:

  • Net flows growth decelerating even as FUA keeps rising (market-driven, not organic)
  • Outflows accelerating relative to inflows (adviser or platform attrition)

platformMargin.title: Platform revenue margin
platformMargin.content:
Platform revenue margin is platform/administration revenue as basis points of FUA -- the fee rate Netwealth effectively charges on the balances it administers.

For Netwealth Group Limited: the margin has drifted down from 33.6bps (FY2023) to 30.7bps (FY2026) as FUA scales and larger accounts negotiate lower rates -- the key question for the thesis is whether FUA growth keeps outrunning this compression.

What to watch:

  • Margin compression rate versus FUA growth rate -- revenue growth needs the latter to beat the former
  • Mix shift toward larger accounts or institutional/managed-account business, which typically carries a lower margin

npatBridge.title: Statutory vs Adjusted NPAT
npatBridge.content:
Net income (statutory) is reported NPAT including one-off items; Adjusted NPAT is management's measure excluding items it considers non-recurring.

For Netwealth Group Limited: FY2026 statutory NPAT absorbed a A$105.2m provision tied to the First Guardian/Brite managed-investment-scheme matter -- a regulatory and client-remediation exposure, not an operating cost. Adjusted NPAT strips this out as the better read of underlying earnings power; the DCF's base FCF is normalised on the same basis.

What to watch:

  • Whether the gap closes to zero in FY2027 (one-off) or recurs (becomes operating)
  • Cash actually paid out against the provision versus the accounting charge

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Netwealth Group Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Netwealth Group Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Netwealth Group Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Netwealth Group Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Netwealth Group Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Netwealth Group Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
